newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RALLYING-SWEDISH RALLY UNCHANGED DESPITE THAW.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SWEDISH RALLY UNCHANGED DESPITE THAW.

text.p: The organisers of the Swedish Rally, which was beginning on Friday night, will still be held on frozen lakes and rivers despite a recent thaw, officials have confirmed.
An unseasonal warm spell has led to surface water forming on the top of the lakes and rivers, though there is still sufficient ice underneath to leave the drivers in no danger.
Temperatures have risen to four degrees centigrade instead of the usual minus 30 degrees and some stages were believed to be threatened.
But officials confirmed on Friday afternoon that the event's schedule would remain unchanged despite unpredictable weather conditions. Teams have been informed.
"We have been told that the rally will run as planned," a spokesman for the Subaru team said. "Although there is surface water, there will be no changes to the stages."

German driver Armin Schwarz, fourth in the season-opening Monte Carlo rally, warned: "Without snow, the rally will be much more difficult. You will need an intimate knowledge of the road and it now means that if you make one mistake your rally will be over."
